analysis.evidence: מִן הַיַּיִן identifies what he drank as some of the wine. The next verb, וַיִּשְׁכָּר, describes the result, “and he became drunk.”
analysis.morphology: The conjunction וַ introduces a third-person masculine singular Qal wayyiqtol. The final ה of שָׁתָה drops out in this shortened form.

draft.change: Add Genesis 3:5 as an example of the existing partitive sense, min-some-of.
draft.definition: With a verb of eating, מִן marks the food of which someone eats a part.
draft.evidence: Genesis 3:5 repeats the suffixed preposition used with the same verb in Genesis 3:3.

analysis.evidence: In וַיֵּשְׁתְּ מִן הַיַּיִן, “he drank some of the wine,” הַיַּיִן names the wine he drank, and מִן marks an unspecified portion of it.
analysis.morphology: Hebrew preposition without a prefix or suffix.
analysis.sense: Partitive, marking what someone eats some of.
